headline: Over 7,300 students killed in road crashes in 7.5 years
summary: Motorcycle accidents are the leading cause of death among students, according to a Road Safety Foundation report.
details: A staggering 7,364 students were killed in road accidents between 2019 and June 2026, accounting for 15.11% of all road crash fatalities in Bangladesh during this period.
According to a press release from the Road Safety Foundation, 3,328 students from schools and madrasas (aged 5-17) were killed, while 4,036 college and university students (aged 18-25) perished.
Motorcycles were the deadliest vehicle type, claiming the lives of 3,841 students. Pedestrians were the second most common victim group, with 1,923 students killed while walking.
The report highlights that younger students (5-12) are more prone to accidents on rural roads while going to school or playing, often involving auto-rickshaws and freight vehicles.
Older students (13-25) are more kills more frequently as motorcycle drivers or passengers on regional roads and highways.
Additionally, 1,237 students died in train accidents, often due to unsafe crossing of rail lines or using headphones while walking along tracks.
The Road Safety Foundation attributes these deaths to faulty roads, unsafe vehicles, lack of awareness, reckless driving, and a failure to follow traffic laws.
The foundation recommends implementing annual road safety campaigns in education institutions, teacher training, and strict enforcement of laws to prevent minors from riding motorcycles.

Motorcycles were the deadliest vehicle type, claiming the lives of 3,841 students. Pedestrians were the second most common victim group, with 1,923 students killed while walking.

The report highlights that younger students (5-12) are more prone to accidents on rural roads while going to school or playing, often involving auto-rickshaws and freight vehicles.

Older students (13-25) are more kills more frequently as motorcycle drivers or passengers on regional roads and highways.

Additionally, 1,237 students died in train accidents, often due to unsafe crossing of rail lines or using headphones while walking along tracks.

The Road Safety Foundation attributes these deaths to faulty roads, unsafe vehicles, lack of awareness, reckless driving, and a failure to follow traffic laws.

headline_marked: 6 [[Bangladeshis killed in South Africa shop fire]]
headline: 6 Bangladeshis killed in South Africa shop fire
summary: The victims were sleeping inside the store when the blaze broke out early Tuesday morning in the Eastern Cape province.
details: Six Bangladeshi nationals were killed in a devastating fire at a shop in the Somo area, located approximately 150 kilometers from Queenstown in South Africa's Eastern Cape province.
The fire broke out around 3:00 AM local time on Tuesday, July 28. The victims were reportedly sleeping inside the store at the time of the incident and died on the spot.
All six victims were residents of the Alirtek and Baktabali unions of Narayanganj Sadar upazila in Bangladesh.
One other person was injured in the blaze and has been admitted to a local hospital for treatment.
The cause of the fire has not yet been determined. Local police are currently investigating the incident.
caption:
6 Bangladeshis killed in a South Africa shop fire while they were sleeping.

Six Bangladeshi nationals were killed in a devastating fire at a shop in the Somo area, located approximately 150 kilometers from Queenstown in South Africa's Eastern Cape province.

The fire broke out around 3:00 AM local time on Tuesday, July 28. The victims were reportedly sleeping inside the store at the time of the incident and died on the spot.

All six victims were residents of the Alirtek and Baktabali unions of Narayanganj Sadar upazila in Bangladesh.

One other person was injured in the blaze and has been admitted to a local hospital for treatment.

The cause of the fire has not yet been determined. Local police are currently investigating the incident.
